citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility has not employed an attending veterinarian (AV) under formal arrangements. During this inspection, the
licensee informed the inspector their previous veterinarian is no longer at the animal hospital identified in their program of
veterinary care (PVC). The AV’s departure occurred in May 2026. While the licensee plans to designate a different
associate veterinarian from the same animal practice, none of these associates conduct house calls. Upon the inspector
contacting the animal hospital, they confirmed their current associates would not be able to visit the facility premises. At
this time, the departed AV was the only associate that conducted house visits.
The written program of veterinary care affirms both entities (facility and attending veterinarian) have a clear understanding
of their respective roles to provide appropriate care for the dog housed on-site. The facility should ensure that the written
program of veterinary care is available for review during all USDA inspections, including all required documented
arrangements outlined in this subchapter.
Correct by September 1, 2026.

Two adult dogs (“Visa”, “Ryver”) and one puppy (“Quest”) housed at the facility did not have official identification as
required by the Animal Welfare Act. While the facility’s preferred form of identification is microchipping, none of the
applicable identification methods have been utilized for these animals.
Approved methods of identification are necessary for APHIS officials to correctly identify animals for inventory, acquisition,
disposition, transport, and health care documentation. The facility shall identify all live dogs under his or her control or on
his or her premises, whether held, purchased, or otherwise acquired as set forth in paragraph (b)(1) or (b)(3) of this
section.
Correct by August 28, 2026.

The facility did not have acquisition records for two young adult dogs (“Ryver”, “Blackie”). Additionally, no disposition
record was available for one adult dog (“Topic”). The licensee looked through all their records during this inspection but
could not confirm the specifics for each record. The licensee acknowledged the required information had not been
recorded in full anywhere else.
Acquisition and disposition records, including offspring born at the facility, are necessary to accurately track and identify
dogs used in regulated activities, as well as aid in the detection of their movement upon relocation to a new site. The
licensee shall make, keep, and maintain records of acquisition/disposition of all animals that fully and correctly disclose
the required information, as outlined in this section.
Correct by August 25, 2026.

One outdoor enclosure housing two young adult dogs did not offer any shelter structures. Though the licensee stated the
previous shelter structure had been removed for cleaning, a shelter housing alternative had not been incorporated in the
interim. Per the licensee, both dogs remain outdoors during the day, bringing indoors nightly and as needed during the
day.
The presence of shelters structures constructed as outlined in this subpart help protect the animals from inclement
weather and variable weather conditions encountered. All shelters housing dogs in outdoor facilities must contain a roof,
four sides, a floor, and provide a wind break and rain break at the entrance to help keep the animals dry and comfortable
in their shelter.
Correct by September 7, 2026.

The facility’s current exercise plan was approved by an attending veterinarian (AV) no longer used by the facility. During
this inspection, the licensee stated they were aware their previous AV departed the animal hospital on file. Since this
event, the facility has not secured a new AV to reflect changes in veterinary approval for the facility’s exercise plan.
An approved exercise plan ensures that adequate exercise opportunities are provided for the dog on-hand and is
appropriate based on its health status and physical needs. The facility shall maintain an appropriate exercise plan that’s
approved by the attending veterinarian and available during APHIS inspections for review.
Correct by September 1, 2026.

The dates of administration for various treatments for two adult dogs at the facility have not been recorded in full:
- One adult dog (“Teaser”) receives oral medication twice daily for a chronic condition. During medical record review, the
last recorded date of administration for Teaser’s medications was July 12, 2026. While the licensee stated she gave the
medications, they informed the inspector they’d forgotten to record them. The licensee confirmed the date of
administration had not been recorded anywhere else.
- One adult dog (“Visa”) received its monthly heartworm preventative for July 2026, but the date of administration was not
recorded by the facility. The licensee looked through all their records during this inspection, but no documentation was
logged. The licensee confirmed the date of administration had not been recorded anywhere else.
Adequate record keeping is necessary to ensure that the guidance of the attending veterinarian is being followed, and
helps the facility verify that medications were administered as directed. The facility must keep and maintain the names of
all vaccines and treatments and the dates of administration given to dogs at the facility.
Correct by August 20, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee and Supervisory Animal Care Specialist.
Additional Inspectors:
KRISTIN NAPOLI, SUPERVISORY ANIMAL CARE SPECIALIST n
